sentences.text:
THIS PETITION IS COMING ON FOR ORDERS, THIS DAY,
THE COURT MADE THE FOLLOWING:
 ORDER
This petition under Section 439 of Cr.P.C. is filed praying to enlarge the petitioner/sole accused on regular bail in Crime No.5/2022 of Davangere Rural Police Station.
2. In the complaint lodged by victim's father, it is alleged that his minor daughter aged about 17 years was kidnapped by the petitioner on 31.12.2021.
FIR was registered against the petitioner for an offence punishable under Section 363 of IPC.
The victim was traced on 13.02.2023.
The accused was arrested on the same day.

The police have filed the charge-sheet against the petitioner for offences punishable under Sections 363, 376(2)(n) of IPC and Section 6 of POCSO Act, 2012 and Section 9 of Prohibition of Child Marriage Act.
3. It is alleged by the prosecution that the victim and the accused belong to the same community and they are related to each other.

On 31.12.2021 at about 1.00 p.m. when the victim was proceeding near the bus stand so as to attend the birthday party of her cousin by name Akshata, the accused by inducing her took her to the house of CW.20 situated in Mudugur Village, N.R.Pura Taluk, in a bus and in the night, he committed penetrative sexual assault on her.

Further, in the month of March,
2022 he took her to a temple and married her and continued to sexually abuse her.
The victim gave birth to a male child on 13.01.2023 and therefore the petitioner has committed the charge sheeted offences.
4. The first informant/father of the victim namely respondent No.2 is represented by a counsel.
He has filed the affidavits of the victim and the complainant.
In her affidavit, the victim has stated that the petitioner has married her only after she attained the age of majority.
She has further stated that the allegations against the petitioner are false.
The victim's father has also stated that the allegations are false and the date of birth of the victim mentioned in the school records is not the correct date of birth.

5. The Learned High Court Government Pleader has submitted that the victim has refused to Sri Halesh vs State Of Karnataka on 22 May, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/169748867/
2 undergo medical examination and therefore there is no medical report of the victim.
6.

sentences.text: I have perused the statement of the victim recorded under Section 164 of Cr.P.C.
She has stated that she married the petitioner without any coercion or force.
7. According to the prosecution the date of birth of the victim is 13.12.2004 and therefore she was a minor aged about 17 years as on the date of incident.
The said date of birth mentioned in the certificate issued by the school authority has been disputed by the petitioner's counsel.
The prosecution has to prove the age of the victim as on the date of commission of the offence, in a full-fledged trial.
The victim has not made any allegations against the petitioner in her statement recorded under Section 164 of Cr.P.C.
The petitioner is already arrested and interrogated.
He is not required for any further investigation.
Investigation is completed and charge- sheet has been filed.
In the facts and circumstances, by imposing suitable conditions, the relief sought by the petitioner can be granted.

Hence, the following:
ORDER Petition is allowed.

Petitioner shall be released on bail in Crime No.5/2022 of Davanagere Police Station,
pending on the file of the Court of Additional District and Sessions Judge, FTSC-I, at Davanagere subject to following conditions:
1. The petitioner shall execute a personal bond for a sum of Rs.50,000/- (Rupees Fifty Thousand only) with two sureties for likesum to the satisfaction of the jurisdictional Court.
